notes:
Brian intends to reuse a billing explanation, and Jonah agrees with its mistaken implication that confirmation immediately changes billing and access across the account. Neither asks for review. The useful contribution is an unsolicited process explanation in the existing self-serve billing thread.

Normally, confirmation records an instruction. The scheduled change applies at the period boundary if its schedule is still current. Invoice finalization and payment are separate events, and confirming a later change does not rewrite a finalized invoice. The relevant exception is an immediate payment-gated upgrade, which can be invoiced before successful payment and application of a pending update.

Winterridge's confirmation is dated September 3. The downgrade applied September 4 at 00:00 UTC. Its USD 200 invoice was finalized open at that boundary and paid at 02:00 UTC. Do not invent a subsecond order between application and finalization. The current paid status does not collapse the sequence into one event. Schedule details are retained in supported subscription metadata, not exposed as a native Stripe Schedule resource. The confirmation predates creation of the resulting subscription and does not establish an earlier subscription or former price.

Billing records do not prove changes to every workspace entitlement or accepted commercial terms. Explain the controlling condition, exception and evidence limits with a short dated example. A shorter grounded correction or direct follow-up to Brian or Jonah is valid. The caption and product-label discussions have visible answers, without establishing settlement or notification delivery.

example_messages.text:
I'd change that wording. Normally, confirmation records the instruction. The new billing setting takes effect when its scheduled period starts, provided that schedule is still current. The invoice covers its own period, and an already-finalized invoice isn't rewritten by confirming a later change.

The [procedure](notion://page/f86cc2b2-0a46-4eb0-b88a-23cb48f40257) has one relevant exception: an immediate payment-gated upgrade can be invoiced first, then take effect after successful payment and application of the pending update.

Winterridge's September downgrade used the normal path. Confirmation was recorded September 3. The schedule applied September 4 at 00:00 UTC. Invoice PM-736B302B8F3B was finalized open at that boundary for USD 200, then paid at 02:00 UTC. Its paid status now doesn't make those one event.

I'd also leave account-wide access out of this promise. [Billing integration](notion://page/ab892350-cd42-5366-a551-2424bc48def8) requires separate product and membership evidence.

important_mistakes: Equate confirmation, application, invoice finalization and payment.
Apply the payment-gated upgrade exception to Winterridge's period-boundary downgrade.
Promise that existing invoices, prices or every workspace entitlement changed.
Invent the previous plan, an earlier invoice correction, a credit or accepted commercial terms.
Treat the metadata as proof of an accessible native Stripe Schedule resource.
Give only a status report or a long record dump instead of explaining the sequence.
Reply only outside the original self-serve billing thread.
Reopen the handled caption or label discussions, or claim their separate uncertainties were resolved.
Describe Brian's update as a request for review or wait for an explicit question despite the visible handoff misconception.
